description: Design and execute an ecological sampling program: define the study area, choose a sampling method (quadrat, transect, point-count), calculate species accumulation, compute diversity indices, and produce the ecological assessment.

steps.description: Define the study area: boundaries, habitat types, accessibility, and known ecological features.

inputs.name: area-description
inputs.desc: Geographic location, maps, and prior survey data

inputs.name: survey-objectives
inputs.desc: Target taxa, ecological questions, and required precision

outputs.name: area-map
outputs.desc: Delineated study area with habitat polygons and access points

outputs.name: stratification-plan
outputs.desc: How the area is divided into strata (habitat types) for sampling

process: Delineate the study area boundary using geographic coordinates.
Map distinct habitat types within the area using aerial imagery or prior surveys.
Identify access constraints (roads, terrain, landowner permissions).
Stratify the area by habitat type for proportional or optimal allocation of sampling effort.

steps.description: Select the sampling method based on the target taxa, habitat, and survey objectives: quadrats for plants, transects for mobile fauna, point-counts for birds.

outputs.name: sampling-protocol
outputs.desc: Method, unit size, replication, and spatial layout

outputs.name: effort-allocation
outputs.desc: Number of sampling units per stratum

process: Match the target taxa to the appropriate method: quadrats for sessile organisms, transects for mobile ones.
Determine the sampling unit size (quadrat area, transect length) based on organism density and mobility.
Calculate the number of units needed per stratum for the desired precision.
Lay out the spatial placement: random, systematic, or stratified-random.

steps.description: Execute the field sampling: record species identities, abundances, and environmental covariates at each sampling unit.

inputs.name: sampling-protocol
inputs.desc: The sampling method and unit specifications

inputs.name: effort-allocation
inputs.desc: Number of units and their locations

outputs.name: species-abundance-matrix
outputs.desc: Sites-by-species matrix of counts or cover values

outputs.name: environmental-data
outputs.desc: Covariates measured at each site (soil, moisture, elevation, canopy cover)

process: At each sampling unit, identify and count all target species (or estimate cover).
Record environmental covariates using standardized protocols.
Note sampling conditions (weather, time, observer) for quality control.
Enter data into a structured matrix format immediately to catch transcription errors.

steps.description: Build species accumulation and rarefaction curves to assess whether sampling effort was sufficient to capture the community.

inputs.name: sampling-protocol
inputs.desc: Effort at each site for standardization

outputs.name: accumulation-curve
outputs.desc: Observed species vs. sampling effort, with confidence bands

outputs.name: richness-estimators
outputs.desc: Chao1, ACE, or jackknife estimates of total species richness

process: Compute the observed species accumulation curve by randomly re-ordering sites.
Fit a rarefaction curve to standardize richness across sites with different effort.
Calculate non-parametric richness estimators (Chao1 for abundance, Chao2 for incidence).
Assess whether the curve has reached an asymptote (sampling is sufficient) or is still rising.

steps.description: Compute diversity indices: species richness, Shannon entropy, Simpson's index, and evenness for each site and overall.

outputs.name: diversity-table
outputs.desc: Each site and stratum with richness, Shannon H, Simpson D, and evenness

outputs.name: diversity-comparison
outputs.desc: Statistical comparison of diversity between habitats or treatments

process: Compute species richness (S), Shannon entropy (H'), and Simpson's diversity (1-D) per site.
Compute evenness (H'/ln(S)) to measure how equally individuals are distributed among species.
Partition diversity into alpha (within-site) and beta (between-site) components.
Compare diversity between habitats using rarefaction-based tests or permutation ANOVA.

steps.description: Produce the ecological assessment report: survey design, sampling adequacy, community composition, diversity analysis, and conservation recommendations.

outputs.name: ecological-report
outputs.desc: Structured assessment report

outputs.name: species-list
outputs.desc: Annotated species list with abundances, habitats, and conservation status

process: Summarize the survey design and effort.
Assess sampling adequacy from the accumulation curve.
Present the community composition and diversity results with figures.
Highlight species of conservation concern and recommend management actions.

description: Detect and correct inhomogeneities in climate station records: compare against neighbors, detect breakpoints, classify causes, adjust the record, and validate corrections.

steps.description: Assemble a set of neighboring climate station records to use as references for detecting inhomogeneities in the target station.

inputs.name: target-station-data
inputs.desc: The climate record to homogenize with metadata (location, elevation, instrument history)

inputs.name: station-network
inputs.desc: Inventory of nearby stations with their records and metadata

outputs.name: reference-series
outputs.desc: Selected neighbor stations' records, quality-checked and complete enough for comparison

outputs.name: reference-composite
outputs.desc: A composite reference series from the weighted average of neighbors

process: Select neighboring stations within a correlation radius (typically 50-200 km for temperature).
Screen each neighbor for completeness and data quality.
Compute distance and correlation-based weights for each neighbor.
Build the composite reference as the weighted average of neighbor anomalies.

steps.description: Detect breakpoints in the difference series (target minus reference): use statistical tests to find times where the mean or variance shifts.

outputs.name: breakpoint-list
outputs.desc: Detected breakpoint dates with confidence intervals and shift magnitudes

outputs.name: difference-series
outputs.desc: Target minus reference series with breakpoints marked

process: Compute the difference (or ratio for precipitation) between target and reference.
Apply a penalized likelihood or SNHT (Standard Normal Homogeneity Test) to detect shifts.
Estimate the timing and magnitude of each detected shift.
Apply a significance threshold to avoid detecting noise as breakpoints.

steps.description: Classify each breakpoint's probable cause by cross-referencing with station metadata: instrument changes, site moves, land-use changes, or observer changes.

inputs.name: target-station-data
inputs.desc: Station metadata including instrument history and site history

outputs.name: classified-breakpoints
outputs.desc: Each breakpoint with its probable cause and confidence

outputs.name: undocumented-breaks
outputs.desc: Breakpoints with no metadata explanation (potentially real climate signals)

process: Match each breakpoint date to the station's metadata log (instrument changes, site relocations).
If a metadata event falls within the breakpoint's confidence interval, classify it as documented.
For undocumented breakpoints, check if multiple detection methods agree (higher confidence of real inhomogeneity).
Flag undocumented breaks that might be real climate shifts rather than artifacts.

steps.description: Calculate the adjustment for each breakpoint: estimate the shift magnitude and apply it to the earlier segment to create a homogeneous record.

inputs.name: classified-breakpoints
inputs.desc: Breakpoints with causes and shift magnitudes

inputs.name: difference-series
inputs.desc: Target minus reference for adjustment estimation

outputs.name: adjustment-values
outputs.desc: The correction applied at each breakpoint (additive for temperature, multiplicative for precipitation)

outputs.name: homogenized-record
outputs.desc: The adjusted climate record

process: For each breakpoint, estimate the adjustment from the mean difference before and after.
Apply adjustments cumulatively from the most recent breakpoint backward.
Use an additive model for temperature and a multiplicative (ratio) model for precipitation.
Preserve the most recent segment as the reference period (fewest adjustments).

steps.description: Validate the homogenized record: check that the adjustments reduced the variance of the difference series without introducing new artifacts.

outputs.name: validation-result
outputs.desc: Before/after variance comparison, remaining breakpoint test, and trend comparison

outputs.name: quality-flag
outputs.desc: Whether the homogenized record passes quality criteria

process: Recompute the difference series using the homogenized record.
Test the corrected difference series for remaining breakpoints (should find none).
Compare the variance of the corrected difference series to the original (should be reduced).
Compare trend estimates from the raw and homogenized records to quantify the adjustment's impact.

steps.description: Write the homogenization report: detected breakpoints, their causes, adjustments applied, validation results, and the final record.

inputs.name: validation-result
inputs.desc: Quality assessment of the homogenized record

outputs.name: homogenization-report
outputs.desc: Structured report documenting the entire process

outputs.name: homogenized-dataset
outputs.desc: The final homogenized record with adjustment flags

process: List all detected breakpoints with their dates, magnitudes, and classified causes.
Present the adjustments applied at each breakpoint.
Show the before/after comparison plots and validation statistics.
Provide the homogenized dataset with metadata flags indicating which segments were adjusted.

description: Interpret soil laboratory results: organize test data, classify soil texture, assess nutrient status, evaluate contamination levels, generate management recommendations, and produce the soil report.

steps.description: Organize soil laboratory results: match sample IDs to locations, verify units, flag results outside plausible ranges, and structure for interpretation.

inputs.name: lab-results
inputs.desc: Raw laboratory data with sample IDs, analytes, values, and units

inputs.name: sampling-metadata
inputs.desc: Sample locations, depths, dates, and land use context

outputs.name: organized-results
outputs.desc: Lab results matched to locations with consistent units

outputs.name: quality-flags
outputs.desc: Results outside plausible ranges or with QA/QC issues

process: Match each lab result to its sampling location and depth.
Convert all results to consistent units (mg/kg for metals, cmol/kg for CEC, etc.).
Flag results that fall outside physically plausible ranges.
Check QA/QC: duplicates within tolerance, blanks below detection, spikes within recovery limits.

steps.description: Classify soil texture from particle size analysis: assign USDA texture class, estimate hydrological properties, and assess structural implications.

inputs.name: organized-results
inputs.desc: Sand, silt, and clay percentages for each sample

outputs.name: texture-classification
outputs.desc: USDA texture class for each sample with position on the texture triangle

outputs.name: hydraulic-estimates
outputs.desc: Estimated water-holding capacity, infiltration rate, and drainage class

process: Plot each sample on the USDA soil texture triangle using sand, silt, and clay percentages.
Assign the texture class (sand, loam, clay, etc.) from the triangle position.
Estimate water-holding capacity using pedotransfer functions.
Note management implications: heavy clays need different tillage than sands.

steps.description: Assess soil nutrient status: compare N, P, K, and micronutrients against crop-specific thresholds, and identify deficiencies or excesses.

inputs.name: organized-results
inputs.desc: Nutrient analysis results (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S, Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B)

inputs.name: crop-requirements
inputs.desc: Target crop's nutrient needs and the region's interpretation guide

outputs.name: nutrient-ratings
outputs.desc: Each nutrient rated as deficient, adequate, or excessive for the target crop

outputs.name: fertilizer-recommendations
outputs.desc: Suggested amendments with application rates based on soil test levels

process: Compare each nutrient level to the regional interpretation guide for the target crop.
Rate each nutrient: low (deficient), medium (adequate), high (surplus), or very high (excessive).
Check nutrient ratios (Ca:Mg, K:Mg) for balance issues.
Generate amendment recommendations using the guide's rate tables.

steps.description: Evaluate soil contamination: compare heavy metals and organic pollutants against regulatory screening levels and background concentrations.

inputs.name: regulatory-standards
inputs.desc: Screening levels for the jurisdiction and land use (residential, industrial)

outputs.name: contamination-assessment
outputs.desc: Each contaminant compared to screening levels with exceedance flagged

outputs.name: risk-classification
outputs.desc: Site classification (clean, potentially contaminated, contaminated) based on results

process: Compare each contaminant concentration to the applicable screening level.
Flag any concentration exceeding the screening level for the designated land use.
Compare to local background concentrations to distinguish natural enrichment from contamination.
Classify the site based on the number and magnitude of exceedances.

steps.description: Score overall soil health: integrate physical (texture, compaction), chemical (pH, CEC, nutrients), and biological (organic matter, respiration) indicators.

inputs.name: organized-results
inputs.desc: Organic matter, pH, CEC, and any biological indicators

outputs.name: soil-health-score
outputs.desc: Composite score with sub-scores for physical, chemical, and biological health

outputs.name: limiting-factors
outputs.desc: The one or two factors most limiting soil function

process: Score each indicator on a common scale (0-100) using established scoring functions.
Compute sub-scores for physical, chemical, and biological health.
Identify the limiting factor: the lowest-scoring indicator that constrains productivity.
Compute the composite score and compare to regional benchmarks.

steps.description: Compile the soil analysis report: test results, interpretations, health score, contamination status, and management recommendations.

outputs.name: soil-report
outputs.desc: Structured report for the landowner, agronomist, or regulator

outputs.name: action-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of management actions with expected outcomes

process: Present all test results in a clear table with interpretations.
Summarize the texture, nutrient, contamination, and health assessments.
Prioritize management actions by impact: address limiting factors first.
Include a timeline for expected improvement if recommendations are followed.

description: Assess water quality from sampling through reporting: design the sampling plan, collect and preserve samples, analyze parameters, compute water quality indices, check regulatory compliance, and produce the assessment report.

steps.description: Design the water sampling plan: select sites, parameters, frequency, and collection methods based on the assessment objectives.

inputs.name: assessment-objectives
inputs.desc: Purpose of the assessment (drinking water, ecological, discharge compliance)

inputs.name: waterbody-description
inputs.desc: Type (river, lake, groundwater), location, and known pollution sources

outputs.name: sampling-plan
outputs.desc: Sites, parameters, frequency, methods, and preservation requirements

outputs.name: parameter-list
outputs.desc: Physical, chemical, and biological parameters to measure with their methods

process: Identify sampling sites: upstream/downstream of sources, at intake points, at regulatory compliance points.
Select parameters based on objectives: physical (temperature, turbidity), chemical (nutrients, metals, organics), biological (fecal indicators, BOD).
Determine sampling frequency: event-based for stormwater, monthly for baseline, quarterly for groundwater.
Specify collection methods, container types, preservation (acidification, cooling), and holding times.

steps.description: Record field measurements at each sampling site: parameters that must be measured on-site because they change during transport.

inputs.name: sampling-plan
inputs.desc: Which field parameters to measure and how

inputs.name: site-conditions
inputs.desc: Weather, flow conditions, and visual observations at the time of sampling

outputs.name: field-data
outputs.desc: On-site measurements: temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, turbidity

outputs.name: field-notes
outputs.desc: Visual observations: color, odor, foam, algae, flow conditions

process: Calibrate field instruments before and after each sampling event.
Measure temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, specific conductance, and turbidity at each site.
Record visual observations: water color, odor, floating materials, algal presence.
Document flow conditions (estimated flow rate, water level) and weather.

steps.description: Compile laboratory analytical results: match to sample IDs, check detection limits, flag QA/QC issues, and produce the results table.

inputs.name: lab-reports
inputs.desc: Analytical results from the laboratory with QA/QC data

inputs.name: field-data
inputs.desc: Field measurements to merge with lab results

outputs.name: compiled-results
outputs.desc: Complete dataset with field and lab results merged by site and date

outputs.name: qaqc-summary
outputs.desc: Blank results, duplicate precision, spike recoveries, and holding time compliance

process: Match lab results to field samples by sample ID.
Merge field measurements with lab results into a single table per site.
Check QA/QC: blank contamination, duplicate RPD, matrix spike recovery, holding time compliance.
Handle non-detects: report as less-than the detection limit, note the method used for statistical treatment.

steps.description: Compute a water quality index (WQI) that combines multiple parameters into a single score for communication and comparison.

inputs.name: index-specification
inputs.desc: Which WQI to use (CCME, NSF, or jurisdiction-specific) and its parameter weightings

outputs.name: wqi-scores
outputs.desc: Index score for each site and sampling event with the qualitative rating

outputs.name: parameter-contributions
outputs.desc: Which parameters contributed most to lowering the index

process: Select the sub-index functions for each parameter (how each value maps to a 0-100 sub-score).
Apply the specified weighting scheme (equal weights or parameter-specific).
Aggregate sub-scores into the composite index using the specified formula.
Classify each score into a qualitative category (good, fair, poor).

steps.description: Check each parameter against applicable regulatory standards: drinking water limits, ambient criteria, or discharge permit limits.

inputs.name: applicable-standards
inputs.desc: Regulatory limits for the waterbody's designated use

outputs.name: compliance-table
outputs.desc: Each parameter with its measured value, standard, and pass/fail status

outputs.name: exceedance-summary
outputs.desc: Number and magnitude of exceedances by parameter and site

process: Match each measured parameter to its applicable standard (acute, chronic, or maximum contaminant level).
Compare the measured value to the standard and flag exceedances.
For exceedances, calculate the magnitude (how many times the standard was exceeded).
Identify patterns: which sites, parameters, or seasons have the most exceedances.

steps.description: Write the water quality assessment report: site descriptions, results summary, index scores, compliance status, trends, and recommendations.

outputs.name: assessment-report
outputs.desc: Structured report suitable for regulators or stakeholders

outputs.name: management-recommendations
outputs.desc: Prioritized actions to address identified water quality issues

process: Describe each monitoring site and its upstream influences.
Present results in summary tables and parameter-specific figures.
Report the WQI scores and their qualitative interpretation.
Summarize compliance status and recommend actions for exceedance parameters.

description: Interpret an NMR spectrum from raw data to structure: process the FID, pick peaks, assign chemical shifts, analyze multiplicity and coupling, integrate for ratios, and propose or confirm the molecular structure.

steps.description: Process the free induction decay (FID) into a frequency-domain spectrum: apply apodization, zero-fill, Fourier transform, phase correct, and reference.

inputs.name: raw-fid
inputs.desc: The time-domain NMR signal (FID) with acquisition parameters

inputs.name: processing-parameters
inputs.desc: Apodization function, zero-fill factor, and referencing standard

outputs.name: processed-spectrum
outputs.desc: Frequency-domain spectrum with chemical shift axis in ppm

outputs.name: processing-log
outputs.desc: Apodization, zero-fill, phase correction values, and reference offset applied

process: Apply an apodization (window) function to the FID (exponential or Gaussian) to improve line shape.
Zero-fill to increase digital resolution.
Apply the Fourier transform to convert from time domain to frequency domain.
Phase correct (zero-order and first-order) and reference the chemical shift axis to the internal standard.

steps.description: Pick peaks in the NMR spectrum: identify each resonance with its chemical shift, line width, and intensity.

inputs.name: picking-parameters
inputs.desc: Minimum intensity threshold, solvent peak regions to exclude

outputs.name: peak-list-nmr
outputs.desc: Each peak with chemical shift (ppm), intensity, and line width

outputs.name: solvent-exclusion-log
outputs.desc: Regions excluded (solvent, reference standard) and their positions

process: Set the minimum intensity threshold above the noise level.
Exclude known solvent peak regions (e.g., CDCl3 at 7.26 ppm for 1H).
Identify all peaks above the threshold with their chemical shift and intensity.
Group closely spaced peaks that belong to the same multiplet.

steps.description: Assign each peak to a functional group based on its chemical shift: consult shift tables and consider the molecular formula if known.

inputs.name: molecular-formula
inputs.desc: Known or proposed molecular formula, if available

outputs.name: shift-assignments
outputs.desc: Each peak assigned to a functional group or structural environment

outputs.name: degrees-of-unsaturation
outputs.desc: Calculated from the molecular formula, constraining possible structures

process: Compare each peak's chemical shift to standard correlation tables for 1H or 13C.
Assign probable functional groups: alkyl, aromatic, olefinic, carbonyl, heteroatom-attached.
If the molecular formula is known, calculate degrees of unsaturation (DBE).
Flag any peaks that fall in unexpected regions for the proposed structure.

steps.description: Analyze the splitting pattern (multiplicity) and coupling constants of each resonance to determine neighboring proton environments.

outputs.name: multiplicity-table
outputs.desc: Each resonance with its multiplicity (s, d, t, q, m) and coupling constant(s) in Hz

outputs.name: connectivity-constraints
outputs.desc: Which proton environments are coupled to each other

process: Determine the multiplicity of each resonance by counting the lines in its multiplet.
Measure coupling constants (J values in Hz) from the line spacings.
Match reciprocal coupling constants to identify coupled pairs.
Use the n+1 rule to infer the number of neighboring protons for first-order patterns.

steps.description: Integrate each resonance to determine the relative number of protons: compute integral ratios and check against the molecular formula.

outputs.name: integration-table
outputs.desc: Each resonance with its integral value and assigned proton count

outputs.name: integral-consistency
outputs.desc: Whether the total proton count matches the molecular formula

process: Define integration regions around each resonance or group of overlapping resonances.
Compute the integral (area under the curve) for each region.
Normalize to the smallest integral and round to find relative proton ratios.
Compare the total proton count to the molecular formula to verify consistency.

steps.description: Propose or confirm the molecular structure by combining chemical shift assignments, coupling patterns, integration ratios, and any 2D NMR data.

outputs.name: proposed-structure
outputs.desc: The proposed molecular structure with atom numbering

outputs.name: assignment-table
outputs.desc: Each NMR peak matched to a specific atom or group in the structure

process: Assemble fragments from the shift and coupling data.
Connect fragments using coupling patterns and degrees of unsaturation.
Verify the proposed structure: predict the expected NMR pattern and compare to observed.
Produce the final assignment table mapping each peak to a specific hydrogen in the structure.

description: Quantify proteins from mass spectrometry data: process spectra, search databases for peptide identification, control false discovery rate, normalize abundances, and identify differentially expressed proteins.

steps.description: Preprocess raw mass spectrometry data: convert to open format, filter noise, deisotope, and extract MS2 spectra for database searching.

inputs.name: acquisition-parameters
inputs.desc: Instrument type, resolution, fragmentation method (HCD, CID, ETD)

outputs.name: processed-spectra
outputs.desc: Cleaned MS2 spectra in open format (mzML or MGF)

outputs.name: preprocessing-report
outputs.desc: Spectra count before/after filtering, noise level, and charge state distribution

process: Convert raw vendor files to mzML format.
Filter out spectra below a minimum intensity threshold.
Deisotope and deconvolute charge states to monoisotopic masses.
Extract MS2 spectra with their precursor mass and charge for database searching.

steps.description: Search processed spectra against a protein sequence database to identify peptides: match observed fragment ions to theoretical spectra.

inputs.name: search-database
inputs.desc: Protein FASTA database with target and decoy sequences

outputs.name: peptide-spectrum-matches
outputs.desc: Each spectrum matched to a peptide sequence with a score

outputs.name: search-statistics
outputs.desc: Number of spectra searched, matched, and unmatched

process: Generate theoretical spectra for all peptides from the database within mass tolerance.
Score each observed spectrum against candidate peptides using a scoring function.
Retain the top-scoring match for each spectrum as a peptide-spectrum match (PSM).
Include decoy database hits for subsequent FDR estimation.

steps.description: Control the false discovery rate: use target-decoy competition to set a score threshold that limits false identifications to the specified rate.

inputs.name: peptide-spectrum-matches
inputs.desc: PSMs from the database search including decoy hits

inputs.name: fdr-threshold
inputs.desc: Desired FDR level (typically 1% at PSM and protein levels)

outputs.name: validated-psms
outputs.desc: PSMs that pass the FDR threshold

outputs.name: protein-groups
outputs.desc: Proteins identified from validated peptides, grouped by shared evidence

process: Sort PSMs by score (best to worst).
Walk down the list, tracking the ratio of decoy hits to target hits (the estimated FDR).
Set the score threshold where the estimated FDR reaches the specified level.
Group validated peptides into protein groups using parsimony principles.

steps.description: Quantify and normalize protein abundances across samples: sum peptide intensities, correct for systematic biases, and handle missing values.

inputs.name: experimental-design
inputs.desc: Sample groups, replicates, and any labeling scheme (label-free, TMT, SILAC)

outputs.name: normalized-abundances
outputs.desc: Protein-level abundance matrix (proteins by samples) after normalization

outputs.name: normalization-report
outputs.desc: Method used, missing value handling, and before/after distributions

process: Aggregate peptide-level intensities to protein-level (sum, median, or top-N method).
Apply normalization to correct for loading and systematic biases (median centering, quantile, or VSN).
Handle missing values: distinguish missing-at-random from missing-not-at-random.
Log-transform abundances for downstream statistical analysis.

steps.description: Test for differentially expressed proteins between conditions: apply appropriate statistical tests with multiple testing correction.

inputs.name: experimental-design
inputs.desc: Which samples belong to which condition

outputs.name: de-results
outputs.desc: Each protein with fold change, p-value, and adjusted p-value

outputs.name: volcano-plot-data
outputs.desc: Log2 fold change vs. -log10 p-value for all proteins

process: Apply a moderated t-test (limma) or similar method appropriate for the sample size.
Compute fold changes between conditions.
Correct p-values for multiple testing using Benjamini-Hochberg FDR.
Flag proteins as significantly changed based on adjusted p-value and fold change thresholds.

steps.description: Compile the proteomics report: identification statistics, quantification quality, differential expression results, and pathway enrichment if applicable.

outputs.name: proteomics-report
outputs.desc: Structured report with figures, tables, and supplementary data

outputs.name: protein-list-export
outputs.desc: Exportable table of all identified and quantified proteins

process: Report identification statistics: total proteins, peptides per protein, sequence coverage.
Present the volcano plot and highlight the most significant changes.
If pathway databases are available, test for enrichment of functional categories.
Export the complete protein list with all statistics for downstream use.

description: Interpret thermal analysis data (DSC/TGA): preprocess curves, identify transitions and mass losses, determine kinetic parameters, quantify composition, and produce the characterization report.

steps.description: Preprocess thermal analysis curves: baseline correct, smooth noisy data, and convert to standard units (normalized to sample mass).

inputs.name: raw-thermal-data
inputs.desc: DSC or TGA data: temperature/time vs. heat flow or mass

inputs.name: sample-metadata
inputs.desc: Sample mass, heating rate, atmosphere, pan type

outputs.name: preprocessed-curves
outputs.desc: Baseline-corrected, mass-normalized thermal curves

outputs.name: preprocessing-log
outputs.desc: Baseline method, smoothing applied, and any anomalies noted

process: Normalize heat flow (DSC) or mass (TGA) to the initial sample mass.
Correct the baseline using tangent or polynomial fitting in non-transition regions.
Apply light smoothing if noise obscures transition features.
Check for artifacts: crucible leaks, sample movement, instrument drift.

steps.description: Identify thermal transitions in DSC data: glass transitions (Tg), melting points (Tm), crystallization (Tc), and decomposition onsets.

inputs.name: sample-metadata
inputs.desc: Expected material type for transition identification context

outputs.name: transition-table
outputs.desc: Each transition with type, onset temperature, peak temperature, and enthalpy

outputs.name: transition-assignments
outputs.desc: What physical process each transition represents

process: Identify step changes in heat capacity (glass transitions) and their midpoint Tg.
Identify endothermic peaks (melting) and exothermic peaks (crystallization, curing).
Measure onset temperature (tangent intersection), peak temperature, and endset temperature.
Integrate peak area to determine enthalpy (J/g) for each transition.

steps.description: Analyze TGA mass loss steps: identify decomposition stages, measure the mass lost in each step, and assign each to a chemical process.

inputs.name: derivative-curve
inputs.desc: DTG (first derivative of mass) for step boundary identification

outputs.name: mass-loss-table
outputs.desc: Each step with onset, end, mass loss percentage, and assigned process

outputs.name: residue-analysis
outputs.desc: Final residue mass and its probable identity (ash, oxide, carbon)

process: Compute the DTG (derivative) curve to identify mass loss step boundaries.
Determine the temperature range and mass loss percentage for each step.
Assign each step to a process: moisture loss, decomposition of organic components, oxidation.
Report the final residue mass and infer its composition from the atmosphere and material.

steps.description: Estimate kinetic parameters for thermal events: activation energy, pre-exponential factor, and reaction order using model-free or model-fitting methods.

inputs.name: preprocessed-curves
inputs.desc: Thermal curves at multiple heating rates (for model-free methods)

inputs.name: transition-table
inputs.desc: Which transition or decomposition step to analyze

outputs.name: kinetic-parameters
outputs.desc: Activation energy (Ea), pre-exponential factor (A), and reaction order (n)

outputs.name: kinetic-model-fit
outputs.desc: How well the kinetic model describes the observed data

process: If multiple heating rates are available, use isoconversional methods (Kissinger, Flynn-Wall-Ozawa).
Plot ln(heating_rate / Tp^2) vs. 1/Tp (Kissinger) to extract activation energy.
If a single heating rate, fit model-fitting equations (nth order, Avrami, autocatalytic).
Report Ea with its uncertainty and note the temperature range over which it is valid.

steps.description: Quantify sample composition from the combined DSC/TGA data: crystallinity from melting enthalpy, moisture content, organic/inorganic fractions.

outputs.name: composition-table
outputs.desc: Component fractions: moisture, volatiles, organic, inorganic, crystallinity

outputs.name: composition-method-notes
outputs.desc: How each fraction was calculated and what reference values were used

process: Calculate crystallinity: measured melting enthalpy / theoretical 100% crystalline enthalpy.
Assign moisture content from the first TGA mass loss step (below 120C).
Assign organic content from mass loss between 200C and 600C (in nitrogen).
Assign inorganic residue from the final mass in air or oxygen atmosphere.

steps.description: Write the thermal analysis report: all transitions identified, mass losses quantified, kinetics characterized, and composition determined.

outputs.name: thermal-report
outputs.desc: Structured characterization report

outputs.name: comparison-data
outputs.desc: Parameters formatted for comparison with specifications or literature

process: Present the DSC and TGA curves with all transitions and mass loss steps annotated.
Tabulate all thermal parameters: Tg, Tm, Tc, decomposition onset, residue.
Report the composition analysis and crystallinity.
Compare to specifications or literature values if applicable.

description: Analyze particle size distribution data: preprocess raw measurements, fit distribution models, compute summary statistics, classify by standard, and produce the gradation report.

steps.description: Preprocess raw particle size data: handle instrument-specific formats, correct for sample preparation artifacts, and compute the cumulative distribution.

inputs.name: raw-psd-data
inputs.desc: Size bins and their frequencies (laser diffraction, sieve, or sedimentation data)

inputs.name: measurement-method
inputs.desc: Instrument type, dispersant, sonication time, and sample preparation details

outputs.name: cumulative-distribution
outputs.desc: Cumulative percent passing vs. particle size

outputs.name: frequency-distribution
outputs.desc: Differential volume/number/mass distribution

process: Convert raw data to a common format: size bins (um) and percent in each bin.
Compute the cumulative distribution (percent finer than each size).
Compute the frequency (differential) distribution for each bin.
Check for multi-modal distributions by examining the frequency curve.

steps.description: Fit parametric distribution models to the data: log-normal, Rosin-Rammler (Weibull), or Gates-Gaudin-Schuhmann, and assess fit quality.

outputs.name: fitted-models
outputs.desc: Each model's parameters, goodness-of-fit (R-squared), and the best model

outputs.name: model-curves
outputs.desc: Fitted cumulative and frequency curves for plotting

process: Fit a log-normal distribution (mean and standard deviation of log-size).
Fit a Rosin-Rammler distribution (characteristic size and spread parameter).
Compare fits using R-squared or sum of squared residuals.
Select the best-fitting model and report its parameters.

steps.description: Compute summary statistics from the distribution: D10, D50, D90, mean, mode, span, and uniformity coefficient.

outputs.name: summary-statistics
outputs.desc: D10, D50 (median), D90, mean, mode, geometric mean, span, Cu, Cc

outputs.name: distribution-shape
outputs.desc: Classification: narrow, broad, bimodal, skewed

process: Interpolate the cumulative curve to find D10, D50, and D90.
Compute the span: (D90 - D10) / D50 as a measure of width.
Compute the uniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10 and coefficient of curvature Cc = D30^2 / (D10 * D60).
Characterize the distribution shape: unimodal vs. bimodal, skewness direction.

steps.description: Classify the particle size distribution according to applicable standards: USCS soil classification, pharmaceutical sieve specifications, or cement fineness.

outputs.name: classification-result
outputs.desc: Standard classification (e.g., well-graded sand, fine silt, USP sieve class)

outputs.name: specification-compliance
outputs.desc: Whether the distribution meets target specifications

process: Apply the standard's classification rules using Cu, Cc, and percentage in each size fraction.
Assign the classification category.
If a target specification exists, check whether the distribution falls within the acceptable envelope.
Note any marginal values that are close to classification boundaries.

steps.description: Write the particle size distribution report: the gradation curve, summary statistics, fitted model, classification, and specification compliance.

outputs.name: gradation-report
outputs.desc: Structured PSD report with plots and tables

outputs.name: gradation-curve-figure
outputs.desc: Publication-ready cumulative and frequency distribution plots

process: Plot the cumulative distribution on a log-probability or semi-log scale.
Overlay the fitted model curve on the data.
Present the summary statistics table (D10, D50, D90, span, Cu, Cc).
State the classification result and specification compliance status.

description: Monitor and analyze a fermentation process: track growth, substrate consumption, and product formation over time, fit kinetic models, compute yields and productivities, and produce the fermentation summary.

steps.description: Log fermentation time-course data: biomass (OD or dry weight), substrate concentrations, product concentrations, pH, dissolved oxygen, and temperature.

inputs.name: raw-measurements
inputs.desc: Time-stamped measurements from sampling and on-line sensors

inputs.name: fermentation-conditions
inputs.desc: Organism, medium composition, aeration, agitation, and control setpoints

outputs.name: time-course-data
outputs.desc: Structured table: time, biomass, substrate(s), product(s), pH, DO, temperature

outputs.name: data-quality-flags
outputs.desc: Missing samples, out-of-range readings, and sensor drift notes

process: Collect all time-point measurements into a single table indexed by time.
Convert OD readings to biomass concentration using a pre-determined calibration curve.
Flag any missing samples, readings outside the sensor range, or suspected contamination events.
Interpolate missing values for minor gaps; flag larger gaps as data holes.

steps.description: Analyze the growth curve: identify lag, exponential, and stationary phases, and compute the specific growth rate.

inputs.name: fermentation-conditions
inputs.desc: Inoculum size and medium for context

outputs.name: growth-parameters
outputs.desc: Lag time, max specific growth rate (mu_max), and time to stationary phase

outputs.name: phase-boundaries
outputs.desc: Time points marking transitions between lag, exponential, deceleration, and stationary phases

process: Plot ln(biomass) vs. time to identify the linear (exponential) region.
Fit a line to the exponential region: the slope is the specific growth rate mu_max.
Determine the lag phase duration as the x-intercept of the exponential fit minus the inoculation time.
Identify the transition to stationary phase where growth rate drops to near zero.

steps.description: Track substrate consumption: compute consumption rates, identify limiting substrates, and detect feed depletion or accumulation events.

outputs.name: consumption-profiles
outputs.desc: Each substrate with its consumption rate in each growth phase

outputs.name: limiting-substrate
outputs.desc: Which substrate is depleted first and when

process: Compute the specific substrate consumption rate (qs) in each growth phase.
Identify which substrate is depleted first (the likely growth-limiting substrate).
Check for substrate accumulation events (feeding faster than consumption).
Compute the biomass yield on each substrate: Yx/s = delta_X / delta_S.

steps.description: Analyze product formation kinetics: growth-associated, non-growth-associated, or mixed, and compute the volumetric and specific production rates.

inputs.name: time-course-data
inputs.desc: Product concentrations, biomass, and substrate vs. time

inputs.name: growth-parameters
inputs.desc: Growth rate for classifying production kinetics

outputs.name: production-kinetics
outputs.desc: Classification (growth-associated, non-growth-associated, or mixed) with Luedeking-Piret parameters

outputs.name: production-rates
outputs.desc: Volumetric productivity (g/L/h) and specific productivity (g/g/h) in each phase

process: Plot specific production rate (qp) vs. specific growth rate (mu).
Fit the Luedeking-Piret model: qp = alpha * mu + beta.
Classify: alpha-dominated is growth-associated, beta-dominated is non-growth-associated.
Compute volumetric productivity: total product / (volume * time) for the entire fermentation.

steps.description: Calculate overall yields and process efficiencies: product yield on substrate, carbon balance, and comparison to theoretical maximum.

inputs.name: time-course-data
inputs.desc: Final concentrations of biomass, substrate, and product

outputs.name: yield-table
outputs.desc: Yp/s, Yx/s, volumetric productivity, and process efficiency vs. theoretical max

outputs.name: carbon-balance
outputs.desc: Accounting of carbon into biomass, product, CO2, and unaccounted

process: Compute product yield on substrate: Yp/s = total product / total substrate consumed.
Compute biomass yield on substrate: Yx/s = total biomass / total substrate consumed.
Calculate the theoretical maximum yield from stoichiometry and compare.
Close the carbon balance: substrate carbon into biomass + product + CO2 should sum to ~100%.

steps.description: Compile the fermentation summary report: growth curve, substrate and product profiles, kinetic parameters, yields, and process recommendations.

outputs.name: fermentation-report
outputs.desc: Structured report with time-course figures, parameter tables, and interpretation

outputs.name: optimization-recommendations
outputs.desc: Suggested changes to improve yield or productivity in the next run

process: Plot the time-course data: biomass, substrate(s), product(s), pH, and DO on a single figure.
Tabulate all kinetic parameters: mu_max, qs, qp, alpha, beta.
Present yield and productivity metrics with comparison to targets or literature.
Recommend process changes: feeding strategy, pH control, aeration, or medium modifications.
